# Hypothesis-driven latency investigation — findings (git-history + 5 experiments)

Investigated "what changed in the last week that makes the gates slow" against the recent
`src/rebar/llm` history and the in-band telemetry (`.rebar/usage.jsonl`, 208 calls after
the two live A/B reviews). Ran experiments to prove/disprove each candidate. **Confirmed
mechanism is provider-independent; the Anthropic→Bedrock migration correlates in time but is
NOT the cause.**

## Confirmed mechanism (H6)
Wall-clock is dominated by **output-token generation volume across many agentic turns**, with
a stable decode rate:
- `corr(duration, output_tokens) = 0.982`; `corr(duration, output/request) = 0.952` — far above
  `corr(duration, input_tokens) = 0.789` and `corr(duration, requests) = 0.807`.
- Decode rate is **~60 tok/s and stable** (single-turn ops 53–89 tok/s; agentic per-request
  median 66 tok/s, min 41 / max 81) — i.e. **no throttle/retry stalls**. Latency ≈
  Σ_passes Σ_turns(output_tokens)/60.
So the cost is the **design** of the code-grounding review: multi-pass (per-criterion finder
fan-out → 106 `plan-reviewer` calls) × tool-using agentic verify (`plan-review-verifier-agentic`
up to 31 turns / 236s / 1.4M cumulative input tokens). This predates the migration.

## Disproved candidates (each with its experiment)
- **H5 — provider raw latency: DISPROVED.** Controlled A/B on ONE plan (epic 992d, per-class
  `REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_MODEL` overrides): single-shot `overlap-judge` bed **5.06s** vs ant **5.22s**
  (within noise, identical tokens/cache); full agentic review bed **428.7s** vs ant **903.0s** —
  Anthropic was *slower*. Provider is not the driver.
- **H1 — repeated/runaway tool calls: DISPROVED.** Across all 95 multi-request calls
  `max_consecutive_repeat = 1` and `tool_calls_distinct ≈ tool_calls` (939/941). The recent
  loop-control cluster (`c827 abort runaway loops`, `f6fc memoize duplicate reads`,
  `windowed distinct-ratio signal`) already suppresses repetition; the turns are distinct work.
- **H3 — `30a2` model-max output budget (Jul 30): DISPROVED as a latency cause.** All 208 calls
  finished `finish_reason=stop`; **zero `length` truncations**; no single request approached even
  the *old* 16k per-turn ceiling (the 2 calls whose *cumulative* output >16k were 19- and 25-turn
  agentic calls, ~900–1000 tok/turn). `effective_max_tokens=max(floor,requested)` is only a
  ceiling, so raising 16k→model-max did not increase output here. 30a2 is a correctness fix
  (prevents rare INDETERMINATE-on-truncation), not a regression.
- **H4 — Bedrock `PromptedOutput` fallback (`895c`, old botocore): NOT a latency driver.** Decode
  rate is provider-independent and stable, so the fallback's extra parse/log noise doesn't move
  wall-clock vs Anthropic native output. (It remains a correctness/observability risk — logs
  `multiple candidates validated … selecting the LAST` — but not a latency cause.)
- **H2 — quadratic input-context growth: real but NOT dominant.** `tok/req` stays roughly flat
  (~10–15k) because prompt caching absorbs the growing prefix (`cache_read` 50–89% of input every
  turn). Input context grows, but it is cheap and generates the weaker correlation (0.789).

## What actually changed in the window (H7 — partial contributors, ranked)
The dominant cost is the pre-existing agentic design; recent commits add turns/output only at the
margin:
1. **`ff64` (Jul 30) — T1 web grounding via a real `web_search` tool.** Adds a network tool-call
   turn to T1-routed passes (genuine turn-adder, but scoped to one criterion).
2. **Criteria enabled to BLOCKING (Aug 5): `G7`, `T3/T10`+T10 DET gate, `T5c` HIGH-class, `T11`.**
   Deepen Pass-2 verification (more verify objects → more output).
3. **New criteria `T15`, `P10/P11` (Jul 30–Aug 5):** +2 criteria (41→43), small finder fan-out add.
4. **NOT regressions:** `30a2` (no-op ceiling here), `9374` plan-first shared prefix + `1dbe`/`dd27`
   caching (speedups), the Bedrock cutover itself (not slower per token).

## Conclusion
The minutes-scale wall-clock is the **inherent, provider-independent cost of the agentic
code-grounding review** (output volume × turns × per-criterion passes). The Anthropic→Bedrock
migration is temporally coincident — it shipped in the same window as the criteria-enablement /
web-grounding / exhaustiveness changes and made Bedrock (with the 895c prompted-output correctness
degradation) the default — but Bedrock is **not slower per token**, so it does not explain the
latency.

## Confirmatory experiment deliberately NOT run (rationale)
A before/after bisect (identical review at a pre-Jul-30 checkout) would further quantify the
marginal contributors, but the baseline predates the `passes.py` completion-seam split (`8705`)
and the model-classes / Bedrock provider seam, so an old build carries schema/provider drift that
would confound an output-volume comparison. The five experiments above already isolate the
mechanism provider-independently, so the bisect is a nice-to-have, not load-bearing.

## Actionable levers for the eventual fix (the real cost centers)
- Cut **turns/output in the agentic verifier** (the 31-turn / 236s cost center): tighten the
  per-criterion tool-exploration budget, or batch criteria per verify call (fewer, cheaper turns).
- Reduce **per-criterion finder fan-out** (106 `plan-reviewer` calls) — batch more criteria per
  finder call (partially done by `730ff31 batch overlap-judge`, extend to the finder).
- Restore per-pass latency telemetry on the sidecar (task 4a40) so this is measured in-band, and
  upgrade botocore ≥1.43.64 to drop the 895c prompted-output overhead (correctness, not latency).

comments.body:
Evidence from [rebar:2876-7958-8dee-4882] bearing on the provider A/B: some gate traffic was
NOT running on the provider it was recorded as running on.

Proven on 2876: the LLM config table was discovered from the ambient cwd / `REBAR_ROOT` instead
of from the gate's pinned code root. Call sites that thread a root
(`workflow/runners.py:129`, `code_review/batch_runner.py:69`,
`plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:99`) resolved Bedrock correctly; sites that thread
nothing (`overlap/judge.py`, `plan_review/__init__.py:_verifier_cfg`, `completion.py`,
`enrich.py`, `epic_bug_screen.py`, `code_review/workflow_ops.py`) silently fell back to the
built-in bare-Anthropic class defaults.

One measured plan-review run shows BOTH in the same process: a successful
`bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-...` call alongside `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` calls.
So a single "Bedrock" gate run could be a MIX of Bedrock and direct-Anthropic traffic, split by
which code path bound the model.

Why this matters for A/B timing specifically: the two providers were being sampled
non-uniformly and invisibly, and the misrouted arm FAILED FAST (0.2-0.4s to a 401) rather than
completing. So pre-fix wall-clock numbers include (a) an unknown share of calls on the wrong
provider and (b) fast failures that shorten some steps while making others retry or degrade.
Either direction of bias is possible; the numbers are not clean.

Recommendation: treat provider-attributed latency collected before change
https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1494 as unreliable, and re-baseline after it
lands. `provider_provenance.ran_model` on the signed verdict is the field that tells you which
provider actually served a run — worth keying the A/B off that rather than off the configured
provider.

comments.body:
## Experiment: fidelity-neutral wall-clock levers (results)

Goal: cut gate wall-clock WITHOUT changing calls/outputs (fidelity). Ran on epic 992d, isolated worktree, per-provider.

**L1 — provider concurrency is free (CONFIRMED).** Anthropic micro-benchmark firing N identical ~2k-output calls at concurrency 1/4/8/12: per-call latency inflation ≤1.03×, aggregate throughput linear (38.8→148.9→283.2→431.7 tok/s). The provider serves parallel calls with no throttling to ≥12.

**L2 — raise the Pass-1 finder worker cap 6→12/16 (REJECTED).** Despite L1, raising the cap did NOT reduce end-to-end wall-clock and broke runs:
- Bedrock w16: **794s** vs 428s baseline, with a 332.9s throttle-stall then failure. (Confounded: a parallel session was consuming shared Bedrock account quota — cross-session contention is itself a real aggravator.)
- Anthropic w12: **947s** vs 903s baseline, FAILED with a cache-write race (`FileNotFoundError` on the ticket-tracker `.cache.json.tmp`→`.cache.json` atomic rename) surfaced by 12-way concurrency.
Root cause it doesn't help: the finders are **not** the critical path — they already overlap inside the pool of 6. The earlier "sum≫max" headroom was an artifact of existing concurrency, not serial waste.

**L3 — the serial `plan-review-verifier-agentic` pass is the dominant cost (CONFIRMED).** In the w12 timeline it was ONE call: 48 turns, 30,399 output tokens, **467.8s**, spanning nearly the whole wall while coach/digest/overlap-judge overlapped. It is decode-bound: ~30k output ÷ ~60 tok/s ≈ ~500s of irreducible decode. Output volume IS the wall-clock (consistent with corr(dur,output)=0.982 from the prior investigation).

**Implication for fidelity-neutral levers:**
- **L4 (RECOMMENDED, untested here):** shard the monolithic verifier-agentic call into N *independent* sub-calls run concurrently. Since provider concurrency is free (L1) and the verifier is the serial bottleneck (L3), splitting its output across N concurrent shards cuts its decode wall ~N× at **identical total output/fidelity**. This is the real lever — parallelize the verifier, not the already-parallel finders. (Verifier is owned by the parallel session; flagging for coordination.)
- **L5 (MARGINAL):** prompt-caching the verifier's ~487k-token input trims per-turn input TTFT but cannot touch the ~500s decode floor — low yield.
- **L2 is a dead end** and additionally introduces a correctness hazard (see linked cache-race bug).

Net: there is **no free wall-clock win in the finder fan-out**. Meaningful reduction requires either sharding the verifier's output across concurrent calls (L4, fidelity-neutral) or reducing the verifier's output/turn budget (a fidelity tradeoff, not free).

# Plan-review and completion-verifier gates run slowly (minutes-scale wall clock); latency is NOT explained by the Anthropic→Bedrock provider switch, but correlates in time with the LLM provider seam migration

## Context / Problem

Since the LLM provider seam migration cut the gates over to AWS Bedrock (epic
[rebar:061c-ecd1-8967-4a76], ADR 0059 landed 2026-08-04 `d416ab9846`; production/local default
set to Bedrock `5bc3a432d7`), the plan-review gate (`rebar review-plan`) and — by shared
mechanism — the completion-verifier gate (`rebar verify-completion`) exhibit minutes-scale wall
clock on real epics/stories. This ticket records the OBSERVED slowness and the result of a
controlled provider A/B, so the next session working the gate does not re-derive it. **It is an
investigation/observability bug: no fix is applied here** — a parallel session owns the
completion-verifier remediation (worktrees `debug-completion-validator`, `impl-10ae-verifier-ctx`).

## Observed evidence (grounded in telemetry + tickets)

**1. In-band telemetry — `.rebar/usage.jsonl` (163 rows, 2026-08-06T20:32Z → 2026-08-07T01:27Z,
`provider=bedrock` on EVERY row — i.e. entirely post-migration; the file is gitignored so no
pre-migration Anthropic baseline was retained).** Per-op `duration_s`:

| op | n | median | p90 | max | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plan-review-verifier-agentic` | 6 | **182.2s** | 276.0s | **276.0s** | up to 19 requests, 463k input tokens in one call |
| `plan-reviewer` | 106 | 21.8s | 60.2s | 99.6s | agentic finder loops |
| `plan-novelty` | 3 | 6.0s | — | 10.0s | |
| `plan-review-coach` | 9 | 5.7s | — | 7.0s | single-turn |
| `ticket-digest` | 9 | 5.5s | — | 7.7s | single-turn |
| `overlap-judge` | 18 | 4.1s | — | 5.4s | single-turn |
| `plan-review-prerequisite-verifier` | 9 | 1.5s | — | 2.6s | |

The cost concentrates in the **agentic** passes (`plan-review-verifier-agentic`, `plan-reviewer`):
75 of 163 calls issued >1 request; the worst issued 19 requests / 276s / 463k input tokens. The
single-turn ops are all <8s.

**2. Controlled provider A/B on ONE plan (epic `992d-9d17-c6ac-4492`, same material, both
providers via per-class `REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_MODEL` overrides; Anthropic key sourced from the
operator env). This isolates provider from plan content.**

- **Single-shot floor ops are provider-identical** (same inputs, same cache behaviour):
  - `overlap-judge`: Bedrock median **5.06s** vs Anthropic **5.22s** (per-call: bed `[5.53,5.67,4.59,4.45]`, ant `[6.08,5.83,4.61,4.40]`); identical `input_tokens`≈4.8k and `cache_read`≈1.3k.
  - `ticket-digest`: Bedrock ~6.4s vs Anthropic ~4.8s.
- **Full agentic review wall clock (after remediating the P1 floor blocker so the review reaches
  the agentic passes):**
  - **Bedrock: 428.7s** (7.1 min), 13 LLM calls, 72 requests.
  - **Anthropic: 903.0s** (15.0 min), 21 LLM calls, 151 requests — i.e. Anthropic was *slower* on
    this sample.
  - `plan-review-verifier-agentic` per-request: Bedrock **31 req / 236.5s (7.6s/req)** vs Anthropic
    **25 req / 374.3s (15.0s/req)**.

**Conclusion of the A/B: provider raw latency does NOT account for the slowness.** On identical
single-shot calls the two providers are within noise; on the agentic passes BOTH are minutes-scale,
and in this sample Anthropic was slower overall. The dominant driver is the **agentic loop
structure** — request count × monotonically growing context (the verifier-agentic call re-sent
~1.4M input tokens across its loop on both providers) — not the Anthropic→Bedrock switch. The
migration correlation is **temporal** (the gates got slow right as the seam/agentic-verifier work
shipped and Bedrock became default), not **provider-latency causal**.

**3. Shared mechanism ⇒ the completion verifier has the same exposure.** Plan-review's
`plan-review-verifier-agentic` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:406` `execution_mode="agentic"`)
and the completion verifier (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:594`
`execution_mode="agentic"`, ops `completion-verifier-evidence` / `completion-verifier-finalizer`)
run the SAME agentic runner with the same per-criterion context accumulation. So the completion
verifier is expected to show the same minutes-scale profile even though it is absent from the
current `usage.jsonl` window.

## Provider-specific aggravators observed (secondary, NOT the dominant cause)

These are real Bedrock-path degradations seen live during the runs, but the A/B shows they do not
explain the bulk of the latency (Anthropic, which avoids them, was still slow):

- **Structured-output falls back to `PromptedOutput` on Bedrock** (bug 895c, `d8adf0f565`): the
  installed botocore cannot send Bedrock's `outputConfig`, so every contract (`TicketDigest`,
  `OverlapVerdictBatch`, `P1Output`, …) routes to prompted JSON and logs
  `parse_structured: multiple candidates validated … selecting the LAST` — extra generation +
  reparse on the Bedrock path only. (`>=1.43.64` restores native output; local env has an older
  botocore.)
- **Bedrock ignores `llm_retry_max_attempts` / `timeout_s`** (bug [rebar:61d8-ff23-8ee0-4289],
  `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` bare `BedrockProvider(region_name=region)` — no
  `botocore.config.Config(retries=…)`, no read timeout). Bedrock uses botocore stock retry defaults,
  which are neither configured nor observable, so a throttle-induced stall on the agentic loop is
  invisible and un-tunable.

## Why this is currently hard to see (observability gap)

Per-pass latency/cost telemetry (`coverage['metrics'] = {det_ms, llm_ms, total_ms, llm_calls}`) is
NOT emitted on the workflow plan-review gate — that regression is tracked open in task
[rebar:4a40-ea6e-d3f7-4af7]. So the slowness above is only visible in the raw `usage.jsonl` sink,
not in the signed sidecar an operator would read.

## Scope (for the eventual fix — NOT done here)

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` — the agentic verifier/finder passes and their per-request
  context growth / request-limit envelope.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` — the completion verifier's agentic passes (same
  mechanism; **owned by the parallel session**).
- `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` — botocore retry/timeout envelope (bug 61d8, already filed).
- botocore floor for native structured output (bug 895c).
- Restore per-pass latency telemetry on the workflow gate (task 4a40) so this is measured in-band.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Root cause of the agentic-pass wall-clock is stated as a specific changeable artifact (request
      count and/or unbounded context accumulation in the agentic runner), grounded in per-request
      telemetry — not attributed to provider raw latency, which the A/B here refutes.
- [ ] A repeatable measurement exists (per-pass `det_ms`/`llm_ms`/`total_ms`/`llm_calls` on the
      signed sidecar, via task 4a40) so a before/after can be asserted rather than eyeballed from
      `usage.jsonl`.
- [ ] The provider A/B conclusion is preserved: an equivalent single-shot op is verified within-noise
      across Anthropic and Bedrock, and the agentic passes are shown minutes-scale on BOTH.
- [ ] The completion-verifier remediation is cross-referenced (parallel session) so the shared
      agentic-runner fix is not duplicated or divergent.
compiled_state.title: Plan-review and completion-verifier gates run minutes-scale; provider A/B refutes Anthropic->Bedrock as the cause (correlates in time with the LLM provider seam migration)
